title: Temperature and wind interactions were uncertain in bird survey records from Canada and the US in 1985-2024
abstract: We tested whether temperature changed the wind association with recorded bird richness in 64,681 accepted roadside surveys from Canada and the US in 1985-2024. We fit four country-period models for the last-minus-first ten-stop taxon count. We controlled for observer-route and state-year effects, survey timing, and weather. The interaction estimates were -0.136 and -0.093 taxa per 5 C per wind code in Canada, and +0.039 and +0.022 in the US. All four intervals included zero after correction for four tests. Route trends, fair-weather limits and categorical wind checks did not resolve a common interaction. The result does not prove that weather effects are separate or absent. Coarse endpoint weather, complete-case selection, shared routes and unmeasured activity or detection limit inference. We did not estimate climate damage or air pollution effects. We preserve a raw-data rebuild check, source hashes, the derived panel, all model results, figures, code and numerical checks.

display.caption: Temperature-wind interaction estimates with four-test intervals. All primary intervals include zero. The right panel uses separate wind-category temperature slopes.
